title: Once-in-a-generation solar eclipse wows millions in UK and Europe
facts: A major solar eclipse occurred across the United Kingdom and Europe on August 12, 2026.
The partial eclipse in the United Kingdom reached its peak shortly after 19:00 BST.
The Moon covered more than 90% of the Sun across most regions of the United Kingdom.
Parts of Greenland, Iceland, and Spain experienced a total solar eclipse.
The path of the total eclipse originated at the northern tip of Siberia in Russia.
The partial solar eclipse began in northern Scotland at approximately 18:00 BST.
The partial eclipse began along the southern coast of England shortly before 18:20 BST.
The solar eclipse reached approximately 95% coverage of the Sun in Cornwall.
Totality occurred in Spain at approximately 19:30 BST (20:30 local time).
Chilean scientist Yasmin Catricheo traveled to A Coruña in north-west Spain to observe the total eclipse.
A total solar eclipse occurs somewhere on Earth approximately once every 18 months.
A total solar eclipse recurs at any single specific geographic location roughly once every 400 years.
The Sun is located approximately 150 million kilometers (93 million miles) from Earth.
The United Kingdom is scheduled to experience a partial solar eclipse with about 45% coverage in 2027.
The next total solar eclipse visible from the United Kingdom will take place in 2090.
